chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Adhina, from Burayd al-Ajli, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

"What is the least by which a servant becomes a disbeliever?" He said: He took a pebble from the ground and said: "That he says to this pebble, 'It is a deity,' and dissociates himself from those who oppose him in that, and attributes to Allah the dissociation from whoever says something other than his saying. This is the Nāsib who has associated partners with Allah and disbelieved, though he does not know it."

key_terms.نَاصِبٌ: Nāsib (one who opposes the Ahl al-Bayt, often used for early Khawarij or Umayyad loyalists)
key_terms.نَوَاة: Deity / God (literally 'kernel' or 'core', used here for divinity)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum act that turns a Muslim into a disbeliever according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the minimum threshold of *kufr* (disbelief) as *al-kufr al-ash'ar* (unintentional disbelief), where one elevates a created object to divine status and rejects dissenters. This highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between major disbelief that expels one from the fold of Islam and minor innovation, emphasizing that rigid adherence to a specific interpretation while condemning others constitutes a form of *shirk* even if done unknowingly.
